set.typical_award_size: Regulatory. The City applies state density bonus law (Government Code 65915) through Implementing Zoning Ordinance Chapter 27, last updated in 2019 (Ord. 2696); Zoning Code Interpretation 2023-01 (September 8, 2023) directs staff to apply state law wherever Chapter 27 conflicts until the code is updated. The Chapter 27 text on the gocodebook mirror (text as of October 4, 2026, code current through Ord. 2907 of September 8, 2025) still shows no amendment after 2019, so no local bonus beyond state law appears to be codified. In November 2022 the City Council adopted a resolution exempting deed-restricted affordable housing projects from the City's facilities, parkland, traffic and open space impact fees (City Housing Finance Analysis, August 2023). Housing Element Program 14 committed the City to establish by December 2023 an incentive package (expedited review, dedicated project manager, Local Housing Trust Fund participation, density bonus beyond state law, waived, reduced or deferred impact fees, streamlined review for 100% affordable projects); adoption of that package was not found.

As of November 10, 2026, confirm with Petaluma Planning whether the Program 14 incentive package and a Chapter 27 update were adopted, and the status of Program 15 (Workforce/Missing Middle).

set.typical_award_size: 50% reduction of three development impact fees (Parkland Acquisition, Park Facilities and Transportation/Traffic) for qualifying deed-restricted affordable housing units, adopted with the 2021 Comprehensive Development Impact Fee Update (Council item June 1, 2021, effective August 2, 2021 or 60 days after adoption). Capital Facilities and Fire Facilities fees are paid at the full rate. Staff estimated the reduction at about $9 million of CIP funding ($7 million parks, $2 million transportation). The FY 2024-25 Development Impact Fee Annual and Five-Year Report (December 9, 2025) fee schedule still carries the 50% rate (note 6). A separate City affordable housing fee deferral program was not confirmed in these documents; state law deferral (Government Code 66007) still applies.
set.per_unit_cap: Not applicable; 50% of the per-unit Parkland, Park Facilities and Traffic fee rates for each qualifying deed-restricted unit.
set.affordability_requirement: Applies per deed-restricted unit (the project does not need to be 100% affordable). Deed-restricted affordable housing means units whose deed restricts occupancy by maximum income, in no case above moderate income as defined in FMC 18.155.020 (generally 120% AMI).
eligible_project_detail: new construction with deed-restricted affordable units
mixed-income projects (reduction applies to the deed-restricted units)
set.next_deadline: No deadline; reduced rates apply when impact fees are paid at building permit.
set.cycle_notes: Rolling. Rates set by the 2021 implementing resolution and adjusted annually by construction cost index.
set.layering_notes: Fee relief stacks with Fund 196 loans and state fee deferral; school (FUSD), water (ACWD) and sewer (USD) fees are outside the City resolution. Alameda County has no countywide fee waiver (county record). fremont.gov returns 403; the 2021 staff report, implementing resolution and the 2025 fee report were read on fremontcityca.iqm2.com.
set.prevailing_wage_basis: No program-specific prevailing wage rule is recorded for this program; the 2021 implementing resolution and staff report contain no wage term. Labor Code 1720(b)(4) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720) counts fees reduced or waived by a political subdivision as public funds, so this relief can make a project paid for in part with public funds. Coverage then turns on project facts and 1720(c): (c)(1) private residential projects on private property not built under an agreement with a state agency, successor agency or housing authority, (c)(3) de minimis (subsidy under $600,000 and under 2 percent of total project cost), and (c)(5)(E) where the public participation is below-market loans on a project with at least 40 percent of units restricted 20 years at or below 80 percent AMI. Other public funds in the deal often decide the question.
set.audit_note: NC audit Nov 10, 2026: earlier text overstated the relief as a 50% cut of all impact fees under FMC 18.290 at 120% AMI. The 2021 implementing resolution (IQM2 item 4360, Exhibit A-1 note 6) limits the 50% reduction to Parkland, Park Facilities and Traffic fees for deed-restricted units up to moderate income; the 2025 fee report confirms it is still in effect. City fee deferral program not found.

reason: Implementing resolution limits the 50% reduction to Parkland, Park Facilities and Traffic fees for deed-restricted units at or below moderate income; Capital and Fire fees are paid in full.
